fixes.why: The card's _why says readings are ordered by when each was articulated, but it puts the continuing-gifts reading first (its organised form dates from the 1900s) and the sign-gifts reading second (argued from the Reformation era and set out in the 1800s). By the card's own rule the sign-gifts reading comes first, and the order as printed favours the reading placed first.
fixes.fix: Swap readings 1 and 2, so the sign-gifts reading (the cessationist label) is first and the continuing-gifts reading (Pentecostal / Charismatic) is second. The open reading stays third. Update _why to match.

fixes.why: 'Open but cautious' contains 'but', one of the weighted words the brief forbids, and 'cautious' implies the other two readings are not careful. Its holders would not choose that word for themselves.
fixes.fix: Label becomes: The gift may be given today, and in the church it is tested, interpreted and put in order

fixes.why: Eastern Orthodox appears in no reading, though its churches do not teach that the gifts have ended. Lutheran appears only in a list inside reading 1's summary, and Anabaptist in no reading at all. Those members differ from the others in the same way the summaries already describe.
fixes.fix: held_by of reading 3 becomes ["Catholic", "Eastern Orthodox", "Lutheran", "Anglican", "Reformed", "Baptist / free church", "Wesleyan / Methodist", "Anabaptist"]. Append to its summary: Eastern Orthodox churches do not teach that the gifts have ended, and they place their use under the discernment of the Church. Lutheran members are found here too, and Anabaptist congregations differ among themselves, some sharing this reading.

fixes.why: The note names 'charism' as the Catholic word only. It is a Greek word the Eastern churches also use, and the card's rule is to name a term as the tradition's own.
fixes.fix: Note becomes: The Greek word for a gift of the Spirit (charisma, 'gifts' in 1 Corinthians 12:28), used across the churches; Catholic teaching uses it of gifts given for the good of the church.

fixes.where: terms: baptism in the Holy Spirit
fixes.why: The note says other traditions apply the phrase to conversion. Wesleyan holiness churches apply it to entire sanctification, a separate work after conversion, and do not link it to tongues. The note leaves that tradition out.
fixes.fix: Note becomes: The Pentecostal and Charismatic phrase for an infilling of the Spirit that many describe as after conversion; other traditions apply the phrase to conversion itself (1 Corinthians 12:13), and Wesleyan holiness churches to entire sanctification.

fixes.why: The summary presents Pentecostal and Charismatic churches as a white American mainstream practice with no reference to the movement's origins in multiracial revival in the United States or to its largest African American churches. That makes the reading read as a fringe, which the card should not do.
fixes.fix: After 'as part of the Spirit's present work,' insert: the movement's first gatherings in the United States were multiracial, and churches of African American origin, the Church of God in Christ among them, are among its largest members;

fixes.why: 1 Corinthians 14:4 is the verse most often cited by this reading for private prayer in tongues, and the card names it only inside the answers and terms. Its Berean text is exact and its place is in the count of eight.
fixes.fix: Replace the 14:5 entry with: {"ref": "1 Corinthians 14:4", "quote": "The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.", "note": "Read as the speaker being built up by the gift, in private prayer."}

fixes.why: 'Set it aside' describes the other readings as setting the gift aside, which their holders would not say of their own position.
fixes.fix: Replace 'and not as reasons to set it aside' with 'and not as grounds for forbidding it'.

summary: The card quotes the Berean exactly in all 28 places and takes no side in its structure, but its readings order contradicts its own history rule, and it omits or mislabels several traditions (Eastern Orthodox, Lutheran, Anabaptist and the African American Pentecostal roots) and the word 'cautious' tilts the third reading. With the eight fixes above, the card could be shown; none of them changes a quote.
